violated_contract: Work that outlives the session or identity it was admitted for must not publish into the state its successor now owns. Bind in-flight work to the session generation that admitted it, re-check after every await, and refuse to publish when the generation has moved. Adopting the current generation is not a fix: it silently attributes stale work to a session that never asked for it.
canonical_prevention: Capture the admitted token before the first await, re-check isCurrent after every await — including error and finally — and refuse to publish rather than recapture. Write any fingerprint or cache only after a current commit succeeds: a finally that recaptures and then records accepted uploads will load the retired session's WAL list into the new one and suppress the next session's server-job progress. Prove it by rolling the generation mid-await and asserting the successor's published state and cache stay empty, with a current-generation control that still loads.
